title: BUDGET AND FINANCE COMMITTEE REPORT and ARTS, PARKS, AND CITY FACILITIES COMMITTEE REPORT relative to the Second Construction Projects Report (CPR) for…
text:
[Council File 26-1124-S1]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Not Been Held - (10 Votes Required for Consideration)]
BUDGET AND FINANCE COMMITTEE REPORT and ARTS, PARKS, AND CITY FACILITIES COMMITTEE REPORT relative to the Second Construction Projects Report (CPR) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-27.
Recommendations for Council action, SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF THE MAYOR:
1. AUTHORIZE the Controller to transfer $11,665,484 between departments and funds as specified in Attachment 1 of the City Administrative Officer (CAO) report dated October 5, 2026, attached to the Council file.
2. In accordance with Recommendation No. 1, AUTHORIZE the Controller to reimburse the General Fund within the Municipal Improvement Corporation of Los Angeles (MICLA), upon CAO approval and receipt of the department requesting labor services, construction materials, and supply invoices for completed work, to include reimbursement for labor services documentation that must contain an hourly breakdown with task descriptions and codes detailing the completed MICLA eligible work, relative to the departmental accounts designated for the following projects:
a. Department of Animal Services (DAS) – Installation of Security Cameras (Item A)
b. DAS – Washer and Dryer Replacement (Item B)
c. DAS – East Valley, Harbor, West Los Angeles, and West Valley Animal Shelter Turf Replacement (Item C)
d. Bureau of Engineering (BOE) – Los Angeles Convention Center (LACC) Expansion and Modernization Project (Item D)
e. General Services Department (GSD) – Access Control Units Replacement (Item M)
f. GSD – Van Nuys Municipal Building Cooling Tower Fencing (Item R)
g. GSD – City Hall East Parking Level P3 Light-Emitting Diode (LED) Upgrade (Item S)
h. GSD – City Hall East Parking Level P2 LED Upgrade (Item T)
i. GSD – Fire Station 69 Shower Pan Replacement (Item U)
j. GSD – Fire Station 107 Concrete Masonry Unit Wall Replacement (Item V)
k. GSD – Replacement of Lighting Controls for Ahmanson Recruit Training Center (ARTC) Rooms 2A and 2B (Item W)
l. GSD – El Pueblo Kiosko Plaza Switchboard Replacement (Item X)
m. GSD – Lighting Control Replacement for the Harbor Animal Shelter (Item Y)
n. GSD – Replacement of Automated Transfer Switch (ATS) for Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) Metro Communications Dispatch Center (Item Z)
o. GSD – Replacement of ATS for LAPD Valley Communications Dispatch Center (Item AA)
p. Los Angeles Fire Department (LAFD) – Security Improvements at Frank Hotchkin Memorial Training Center (Item II)
q. LAFD –Training Bureau Electrical Installation (Item JJ)
r. Los Angeles Zoo (Zoo) – Chimpanzees Habitat Rehabilitation (Item LL)
s. Zoo – Sea Life Cliff Holding Pools Liner and Flooring Replacement (Item MM)
3. REAUTHORIZE a total of $3,274,894 in MICLA funding included in the FY 2026-27 Adopted Budget for municipal facilities projects (Item J).
4. AUTHORIZE the establishment of a new appropriation account entitled Seventh Street Body Shop in the amount of $488,853 within the MICLA Fund No. 298/40, Account No. To Be Determined (TBD) - Seventh Street Body Shop (Item L).
5. REAUTHORIZE the use of up to $620,494 in MICLA funding from 2023-24 for the Seventh Street New Body Shop project that has expired; and, REAUTHORIZE continued use of these funds beyond the City’s MICLA Three-Year Spending policy (Item GG).
6. REAUTHORIZE the use of up to $150,652 in 2023-24 MICLA funding authority (Fund No. 298/40, Account No. 40YFFS, Fire Fencing and Security Enhancements) that has expired; and, AUTHORIZE the continued use of these funds beyond the City’s MICLA Three-Year Spending Policy (Item II).
7. AUTHORIZE the CAO to make technical corrections, as necessary, to the transactions authorized through said CAO report, as required to implement the intent of those transactions.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
The CAO reports that the recommendations stated in the report include transfers, appropriations, and authority for expenditures totaling $11.7 million. This consists of $1.6 million from various special funds, $4.4 million in MICLA funds, $5.0 million in Capital and Technology Improvement Expenditure Program (CTIEP) funds, and $0.7 million in general funds. All transfers and appropriations are based on existing funds, reimbursements, or revenues. There is no additional General Fund impact for operations and maintenance as a result of these recommendations. Debt impact statement The CAO reports that the issuance of MICLA debt is a General Fund obligation. The proposed MICLA funding for the capital improvement projects (Items J, L, and GG) would cause the City to borrow $4.4 million at an approximate 5.5 percent interest rate over a period of 20 years. The total estimated debt service for these MICLA- funded projects is $7.4 million, including interest of approximately $3.0 million. The estimated average annual debt service is $0.4 million over a period of 20 years. Actual interest rates may differ as rates are dependent on market conditions at the time of issuance. The CAO's Office cannot fully predict what interest rates will be in the future. In accordance with the City's Debt Management Policy, the City has an established debt ceiling to guide the evaluation of the affordability for future debt. The debt ceiling for non-voted direct debt as a percentage of General Fund revenues is six percent. The 2026-27 non-voter-approved debt service ratio is 2.40 percent. The issuance of MICLA debt for these projects will not cause the City to exceed the six percent non-voter-approved debt limit. Financial policies The CAO reports that the recommendations stated in the report comply with the statement City’s Financial Policies in that appropriations for funds are limited to available cash balances needed to fund ongoing maintenance, programming, project shortfalls, and critical repairs or operational needs in the current budget year.
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
summary: The City Administrative Officer is reporting on the second construction projects report for fiscal year 2026-27, referred to the Arts, Parks and City Facilities and Budget and Finance committees.
